190	## Step 3 — Refresh the registry **[T1 — chained tail of Step 2]**
191	
192	This is already the last segment of the [canonical T1 chain](#canonical-t1-chain--issue-this-as-one-bash-call) above. Standalone:
193	
194	```bash
195	uip maestro flow registry pull                          # refresh local cache (expires after 30 min)
196	```
197	
198	**Parallel `registry get`** — in the same T1 assistant message, emit one separate `Bash` per OOTB node type whose definition you'll inline in T2. **Always fetch `core.control.end`** — `flow init` does not scaffold one (see Step 4):
199	
200	```bash
201	uip maestro flow registry get core.control.end --output json
202	```
203	
204	> **Auth note**: Without `uip login`, registry shows OOTB nodes only. After login, tenant-specific connector and resource nodes are also available. **In-solution sibling projects** are always available via `--local` without login — see below.
205	
206	### Select the node type for each external service (runs even when full planning is skipped)
207	
208	Calling a named external service (Slack, open-meteo, Stripe, any REST API)? **Search first — never guess the node type from the brand name:**
209	
210	```bash
211	uip maestro flow registry search "<service>" --output json --output-filter "[*].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName,Description:Description,AvailableOnTenant:AvailableOnTenant}"
212	```
213	
214	Then pick the first match down this ladder:
215	
216	1. **Curated connector activity** (`uipath.connector.<key>.<op>` in the results) → use it.
217	2. **Connector exists but no activity for what you need** → `core.action.http.v2` (connector mode).
218	3. **No connector at all** → `core.action.http.v2` (manual mode).
219	4. **No API** (desktop app) → [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md).
220	
221	Manual HTTP is the **bottom of the ladder** — only the search returning no connector authorizes it. Picking it without searching is the brand-name shortcut forbidden by [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal).
222	
223	**In-solution discovery (no login required):**
224	
225	```bash
226	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json     # discover sibling projects in the same .uipx solution
227	uip maestro flow registry search "<keyword>" --local --output json  # keyword search across in-solution nodes
228	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json  # get full manifest for a local node
229	```
230	
231	Run from inside the flow project directory. Returns the same manifest format as the tenant registry. Use `--local` to wire in-solution resources (RPA, agents, flows, API workflows) without publishing them first. `search --local` omits `AvailableOnTenant` — drop it from `--output-filter` projections.
232	
233	## Step 4 — Build the flow **[T2]**
234	
235	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
236	
237	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
238	
239	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
240	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
241	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
242	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
243	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
244	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
245	
246	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)).
247	
248	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
249	
250	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
251	
252	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
253	
254	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
255	|---|---|---|
256	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
257	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. Empty after `flow init` (`\n  "edges": []`); the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
258	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
259	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in `init`-scaffolded flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
260	
261	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
262	
263	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
264	
265	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
266	
267	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
268	
269	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
270	
271	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).
272	
273	### Node ownership recap
274	
275	> **Before each node, classify it as user-owned or CLI-owned (see [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)). Connector activities, connector triggers, and `core.action.http.v2` are CLI-only — use `uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`, never Edit. Hand-writing these will fail `flow validate`.**
276	
277	Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` directly in the project root. The `bindings_v2.json` file is also in the project root for resource bindings.
278	
279	> **Tool selection by ownership.** Use `Edit` for in-place changes to user-owned nodes; `Write` only when ≥70% of nodes change. For CLI-owned nodes (above), use `uip maestro flow node add` + `node configure` — see the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for the full configuration workflow. Inline-agent project scaffolding uses `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`, but inline-agent flow node/wiring edits are direct `.flow` JSON (the agent node itself is user-owned).
280	
281	Read [editing-operations.md](editing-operations.md) for strategy selection and per-operation recipes.
282	
283	> **Self-check before each mutation:** name the tool you're about to use. If the answer isn't `Edit`, `Write`, or `uip maestro flow ...` — STOP and ask the user (per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). `python`, `node`, `jq`, `sed`, `awk`, and shell heredocs are a last resort and require explicit user approval after you've surfaced the trade-offs. See [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder).
284	
285	For each node type, follow the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for node-specific inputs, JSON structure, and configuration. The operations guides cover the mechanics (how to add/remove/wire); the plugins cover the semantics (what inputs and model fields each node type needs).
286	
287	## Step 5 — Validate **[T3 — chain with Step 6, plus any T1 `node configure`]**
288	
289	### Canonical T3 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
290	
291	```bash
292	uip maestro flow node configure "<ProjectName>.flow" "<httpNodeId>" --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>' --output json \
293	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
294	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json
295	```
296	
297	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). Tail-append one `node configure` per CLI-owned node added in T1, using the node IDs captured from T1's chained output. Drop the entire `node configure` segment if no CLI-owned nodes exist.
298	
299	> **The plugin `impl.md` is authoritative — follow its full procedure, not just its `--detail` schema, and let it override this turn map.** A plugin may prescribe steps the three-turn collapse does not show — most importantly a **pre-`configure` live fetch** whose output you must read before you can author `--detail` (the value depends on the live response, so it cannot be guessed or copied from a doc example). When `impl.md` defines such a step, run it in its **own turn before T3** and build `--detail` from its result; do not batch it into the chain, skip it, or hand-author the payload. An empty or static base response is expected for these steps and is not a signal the step is unavailable. This is general to every CLI-owned node type — defer to the owning `impl.md` rather than assuming static config.
300	
301	**On validate failure:** one `Edit` turn to fix, then re-chain `validate && format` in one Bash. Do not validate after every individual Edit during T2 — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
302	
303	> **A passing exit code with warnings is NOT done.** `flow validate` returns 0 even when `Data.Warnings` is non-empty — read the warnings, don't just check the exit code. The connector-keyword warning (`node "…" mentions the "<connector>" connector keyword but uses the generic Managed HTTP type core.action.http.v2 with no connection binding`) means the flow took the brand-name shortcut and will run against an undefined endpoint at debug time — resolve it by switching to the connector before reporting the flow complete (see [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) and the anti-pattern list). Treat this class of warning as a build failure for your own definition of "done."
304	
305	### Common error categories
306	
307	- **Missing targetPort** — every edge needs a `targetPort` string
308	- **Missing definition** — every `type:typeVersion` in nodes needs a matching `definitions` entry
309	- **Invalid node/edge references** — `sourceNodeId`/`targetNodeId` must reference existing node `id`s
310	- **Duplicate IDs** — node and edge `id`s must be unique
311	
312	## Step 6 — Format node layout **[T3 — chained tail of Step 5]**
313	
314	This is the last segment of the [canonical T3 chain](#canonical-t3-chain--issue-this-as-one-bash-call) above. After validation passes, format must run before publishing or debugging (see "Always run `flow format` after edits" in [the Author capability index](../CAPABILITY.md)). Format:
315	
316	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) using ELK with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
317	- Sets each non-stickyNote node's `size` by its canvas shape so Studio Web renders it correctly: inline agents (`shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`, containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`, everything else (incl. referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>`) → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }` (skipping this leaves stale dimensions intact and produces misshapen nodes — the MST-9061 failure mode)
318	- Recurses into subflows and rewrites `subflows[<id>].layout`
319	- Backfills missing `position`/`size` entries
320	
321	Standalone (only if not chained from Step 5):
322	
323	```bash
324	uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow --output json
325	```
326	
327	## Completion Output
328	
329	When you finish building the flow, report to the user:
330	
331	1. **File path** of the `.flow` file created
332	2. **What was built** — summary of nodes added, edges wired, and logic implemented
333	3. **Validation status** — whether `flow validate` passes (or remaining errors if unresolvable)
334	4. **Format status** — confirm `flow format` was run
335	5. **Mock placeholders** — list any `core.logic.mock` nodes that need to be replaced, and which skill to use
336	6. **Missing connections** — any connector nodes that need connections the user must create
337	7. **What's next** — ask the user, presenting the dropdown below (see the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md))
338	
339	### What's next dropdown
340	
341	Authoring terminates here. Each option below hands off to Operate — read [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md) for the command sequence.
342	
343	| Option | What it does |
344	| --- | --- |
345	| **Publish to Studio Web** (default) | Push the solution to Studio Web so the user can visualize, edit, and publish from the browser. |
346	| **Debug the solution** | Execute the flow end-to-end against real systems. Confirm consent first — debug has real side effects (see the consent-before-debug rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). |
347	| **Deploy to Orchestrator** | Pack and publish directly to Orchestrator (bypasses Studio Web). Only when explicitly chosen — see [/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform). |
348	| **Something else** | Last option. Accept free-form string input and act on it (e.g., "just leave it", "pack but don't publish", "upload to a different tenant"). |
349	
350	Do not run any of these actions without explicit user selection. Once the user picks an option, read [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md) and follow that capability's flow — do not run operate commands from inside this doc.
351

commands.result_summary:
1	# HTTP Request Node — Implementation
2	
3	This page is the entry point for implementing a managed HTTP node. Pick your auth mode below, then follow the matching walkthrough end-to-end. The "Shared Reference" section is an appendix — the mode walkthroughs already inline what you need to act, and link here only for full rationale and extended examples.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated.
10	
11	## Pick a Mode
12	
13	| Mode | Use when | Walkthrough |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Connector** | Target system has an IS connector — auth via an existing IS connection (OAuth/API key) | [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, public/no-auth API, or quick prototyping | [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md) |
17	
18	> **Mode fallback — auto-try, then confirm.** Prefer a curated connector activity first; if none, use connector mode; if connector mode cannot be configured (connector lacks HTTP request support — `HasHttpRequest` false — or no usable IS connection), fall through to manual mode automatically. Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so confirm the switched mode with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md — Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
19	
20	The `--detail` payload differs in two places between modes: `authentication` (`"connector"` vs `"manual"`), and the connector-binding fields `targetConnector` / `connectionId` / `folderKey` (connector mode only; `url` is then relative to the connector base, vs. an absolute URL in manual mode). Everything else (node add, dynamic values, branches, edges, debug) is shared.
21	
22	## Critical: Use `node configure`
23	
24	> **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, or connection resource files.** Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — it builds everything from a simple `--detail` JSON. Hand-written configurations miss the `essentialConfiguration` block and fail at runtime. `core.action.http.v2` is CLI-owned per [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) (same envelope rules as connector activities).
25	
26	## Registry validation
27	
28	```bash
29	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.http.v2 --output json
30	```
31	
32	Confirm in `Data.Node.handleConfiguration`: target port `input`, source ports `branch-{item.id}` (dynamic, `repeat: inputs.branches`) and `default`. Also confirm `Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling: true` — HTTP v2 participates in the implicit `error` port pattern shared by every action node (see [Action Node Structure](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md)). Model `serviceType` is `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest`.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Shared Reference (appendix)
37	
38	The mode walkthroughs link into the sections below for full rationale and extended examples. You do not need to read this section in order — jump directly from the walkthrough link that brought you here.
39	
40	### Add the node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
44	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance to `nodes[]`, registers the `variables.nodes` entries, and inserts a placeholder in `layout.nodes` — all in code, byte-for-byte from the registry (including `typeVersion`, which the CLI pulls from the manifest's `version` field; do not hardcode it). Save the returned node ID — both walkthroughs reuse it.
48	
49	The CLI initializes `inputs` from the manifest's `inputDefaults`:
50	
51	```json
52	"inputs": {
53	  "branches": [],
54	  "timeout": "PT15M",
55	  "retryCount": 0,
56	  "swaggerDefinition": null,
57	  "detail": {}
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`inputs.detail` is populated by the configure step (next). The inputs-level siblings — `branches`, `timeout`, `retryCount` — are set at `node add` time via `--input`:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
65	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
66	  --input '{
67	    "timeout": "PT30M",
68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
71	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
72	    ]
73	  }' --output json
74	```
75	
76	- `timeout` — ISO 8601 duration (e.g. `PT15M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`). Default `PT15M`.
77	- `retryCount` — integer. Default `0`.
78	- `branches` — see [Conditional branches](#conditional-branches) below.
79	
80	> **Do not hand-author the `core.action.http.v2` definition, and do not `Edit` `inputs.*` after the fact.** Use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for branches/timeout/retryCount) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths.
81	
82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	When an HTTP node has an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly.
176	
177	```json
178	{
179	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
180	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
181	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
182	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
183	  "targetPort": "input"
184	}
185	```
186	
187	### Debug
188	
189	| Error | Cause | Fix |
190	| --- | --- | --- |
191	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
192	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
193	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
194	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
195	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
196	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
197	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
198	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |
199

1	# HITL Node — Implementation
2	
3	Two node types implement human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Choose based on whether you need an inline form or an existing deployed app.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Option 1 — `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (Inline Schema — OOTB)
8	
9	This is the preferred option. No registry pull, no app publishing, no tenant dependency. Write the node directly into the `.flow` file as JSON.
10	
11	**Full implementation guide, JSON examples, and schema conversion rules:**
12	→ [`uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill — hitl-node-quickform.md](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-quickform.md)
13	
14	> **Note:** Skills are self-contained. This cross-skill reference is for documentation context only. The agent uses the `uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill to implement HITL nodes. This implementation guide is for implementation-phase topology resolution only — not for schema design or node writing.
15	
16	### Adding / Editing
17	
18	For add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). **Use `Edit` / `Write` for HITL node authoring.** Do not use the dedicated HITL CLI for this non-carve-out structural edit. Wire the `outcome-completed` port after adding the node.
19	
20	### Quick Reference
21	
22	**Node JSON (minimum viable):**
23	
24	```json
25	{
26	  "id": "hitlReview1",
27	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form",
28	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
29	  "display": { "label": "Invoice Review" },
30	  "inputs": {
31	    "schema": {
32	      "schemaId": "<uuid>",
33	      "fields": [
34	        { "id": "invoiceid", "label": "Invoice ID", "type": "text",   "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice.output.invoiceId" },
35	        { "id": "amount",    "label": "Amount",     "type": "number", "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice.output.amount" },
36	        { "id": "decision",  "label": "Decision",   "type": "text",   "direction": "output", "variable": "vars.decision" }
37	      ],
38	      "outcomes": [
39	        { "id": "approve", "name": "Approve", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true,  "action": "Continue" },
40	        { "id": "reject",  "name": "Reject",  "type": "string", "isPrimary": false, "action": "End" }
41	      ]
42	    },
43	    "recipient": { "channels": ["Email", "ActionCenter"], "connections": {}, "assignee": { "type": "group" } },
44	    "priority": "Low"
45	  },
46	  "outputs": {
47	    "output": {
48	      "type": "object",
49	      "description": "Task result data",
50	      "source": "=result",
51	      "var": "output",
52	      "properties": {
53	        "decision": { "type": "string" },
54	        "Action":   { "type": "string", "enum": ["Approve", "Reject"], "default": "Approve" }
55	      }
56	    },
57	    "status": {
58	      "type": "string",
59	      "description": "Task completion status",
60	      "source": "=result.Action",
61	      "var": "status",
62	      "enum": ["Approve", "Reject"],
63	      "default": "Approve"
64	    }
65	  }
66	}
67	```
68	
69	**Field format rules:**
70	- **Input fields**: `binding: "vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>"` (raw path, no `=js:$` prefix). No `variable` property on input fields.
71	- **Output fields**: `variable: "vars.<globalName>"` (`vars.` prefix required). No `binding`.
72	- **InOut fields**: both `binding` and `variable`, same formats as above.
73	- `schemaId` (not `id`) at the schema level — generate a fresh UUID.
74	- `typeVersion` — always `"1.0"` for `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`. **Do not run `registry get` to derive this value; do not use `"1.1"` or any other version.** The OOTB HITL node version is stable at `1.0`.
75	- No `model` block on node instances — only the definition carries it.
76	
77	**outputs block**: only `output` (with `properties` for output/inOut fields + `Action` outcome) and `status` (with `enum`/`default` from outcomes). No per-field `custom: true` entries.
78	
79	**Ports:** `input` (target) → `outcome-completed` (source, label: Completed)
80	
81	**Output variables:**
82	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — object with all `output` / `inOut` field values, keyed by **field `id`**
83	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldId}` — individual field value (e.g. `$vars.hitlReview1.output.decision`)
84	- `$vars.{nodeId}.status` — selected outcome name (e.g. `"Approve"`, `"Reject"`)
85	- `$vars.{globalId}` — workflow-global alias; `globalId` is `field.variable` with `vars.` stripped. **Do not use this in scripts — always use `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldId}` instead.**
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Option 2 — App-Based HITL (`uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app`)
90	
91	Use when there is an existing deployed Action Center app that should serve as the task form.
92	
93	### Discovery
94	
95	**CLI (primary path):**
96	
97	```bash
98	uip solution resources list --kind App --output json
99	```
100	
101	Returns all Action Center app types (`vB Action`, `workflow Action`, `Coded Action`, `JS Action`). Filter by app name. Then retrieve the configuration:
102	
103	```bash
104	uip solution resources get <key> --output json
105	```
106	
107	**Direct API fallback (if CLI unavailable):**
108	
109	```
110	GET {BASE_URL}/{ORG}/studio_/backend/api/resourcebuilder/solutions/{SOLUTION_ID}/resources/search
111	  ?kind=app&pageSize=25&projectKey={PROJECT_KEY}&includeSolutionResources=true
112	  &types=VB%20Action&types=Workflow%20Action&types=Coded%20Action&types=CodedAction&types=JS%20Action
113	```
114	
115	Full step-by-step (app search → retrieve-configuration → resource files → reference registration → debug overwrites) → **[hitl-node-apptask.md](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-apptask.md)**
116	
117	### Node JSON (Quick Reference)
118	
119	```json
120	{
121	  "id": "invoiceReview1",
122	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app",
123	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
124	  "display": { "label": "Invoice Review" },
125	  "inputs": {
126	    "recipient": { "channels": ["ActionCenter"], "connections": {}, "assignee": { "type": "group" } },
127	    "app": {
128	      "displayName": "Invoice Approval",
129	      "name": "Invoice Approval",
130	      "key": "<app.key>",
131	      "folderPath": "Shared",
132	      "inputSchema": {
133	        "type": "object",
134	        "properties": {
135	          "<paramName>": { "type": "string" }
136	        }
137	      },
138	      "outputSchema": {
139	        "type": "object",
140	        "properties": {
141	          "<outputName>": { "type": "string" }
142	        }
143	      }
144	    },
145	    "appInputBindings": {
146	      "<inputParamName>": "=vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>",
147	      "<inputParamName2>": "=metadata.InstanceId"
148	    },
149	    "schema": {
150	      "fields": [],
151	      "outcomes": [{ "id": "submit", "name": "Submit", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true, "action": "Continue" }]
152	    },
153	    "priority": "Medium"
154	  },
155	  "outputs": {
156	    "output": {
157	      "type": "object",
158	      "description": "Task result data",
159	      "source": "=result",
160	      "var": "output",
161	      "properties": {
162	        "Action": { "type": "string", "enum": ["Submit"], "default": "Submit" }
163	      }
164	    },
165	    "status": {
166	      "type": "string",
167	      "description": "Task completion status",
168	      "source": "=result.Action",
169	      "var": "status",
170	      "enum": ["Submit"],
171	      "default": "Submit"
172	    }
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	**`typeVersion`** — fill in the version returned by `uip maestro flow registry get <appKey>` for the specific deployed app. Unlike QuickForm (always `"1.0"`), AppTask version varies per app definition.
178	
179	**`inputs.app`**: `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` are JSON Schema objects (`{ "type": "object", "properties": { ... } }`), **not arrays**.
180	
181	**`inputs.appInputBindings`** — maps app input parameter names to binding expressions. Format: `"=vars.<path>"` (with `=` prefix, no `js:`). Key = parameter name from `inputSchema.properties`. Without this, all input fields appear blank.
182	
183	### If the app does not exist yet
184	
185	Note as `[CREATE NEW] <description>` in the node table and use `core.logic.mock` as a placeholder. The app itself is out of scope for this skill — use the `uipath-coded-apps` skill to build it.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## Common Pattern — Human-in-the-Loop
190	
191	```text
192	Manual Trigger -> RPA Process (extract) -> HITL (review) -> Decision (approved?) ->
193	  true: Script (submit) -> End
194	  false: End
195	```
196	
197	## Debug
198	
199	| Error | Cause | Fix |
200	| --- | --- | --- |
201	| Node type not found in registry (Option 2) | App not published or registry stale | If in same solution: `uip maestro flow registry list --local`. Otherwise: `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
202	| Task never completes | Human hasn't submitted the form | Check task assignment in Orchestrator |
203	| Output missing expected fields | App form doesn't match expected schema | Verify app form fields match what the flow expects |
204	| `outcome-completed` port unwired (Option 1) | Missing edge on output handle | Wire the `outcome-completed` output handle — an unwired `outcome-completed` blocks the flow indefinitely |
205

1	# HTTP Request Node — Manual Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when there is no IS connector for the target service, the API needs no auth (or auth you pass yourself in headers), or you are prototyping against an arbitrary REST endpoint. For connector-managed auth, use [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) instead.
4	
5	**No connection lookup required.** Manual mode uses `ImplicitConnection` — there are no IS bindings.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–4 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Step 2 reuses it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 2 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
17	
18	## Step 2 — Configure the node
19	
20	> **Find missing values first.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, resolve any values the agent doesn't have (IDs from names, required body fields, response shape, …). See [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md).
21	
22	```bash
23	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
24	  --detail '{
25	    "authentication": "manual",
26	    "method": "GET",
27	    "url": "https://api.example.com/endpoint",
28	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
29	  }' --output json
30	```
31	
32	The CLI:
33	
34	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (manual auth, `ImplicitConnection`, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
35	- Does **not** generate `bindings_v2.json` or a connection resource file — manual mode needs neither
36	
37	`url` must be a full URL (scheme + host + path). For auth headers you control, pass them under `headers`:
38	
39	```bash
40	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
41	  --detail '{
42	    "authentication": "manual",
43	    "method": "GET",
44	    "url": "https://api.example.com/me",
45	    "headers": {"Authorization": "=js:`Bearer ${$vars.apiToken}`"}
46	  }' --output json
47	```
48	
49	**Dynamic values:** HTTP input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
50	
51	## Step 3 — (Optional) Response branches
52	
53	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 4 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
54	
55	## Step 4 — Wire edges
56	
57	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 3 entry). Wire `default` to the next node and `error` to a handler — without an `error` edge, a failed call faults the flow.
58	
59	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
60	
61	## Debug
62	
63	See [impl.md — Debug](impl.md#debug). For manual mode, watch for `ImplicitConnection` errors — they signal a missing `authentication: "manual"` flag or a non-URL `url` value.
64

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	
43	## Common patterns
44	
45	### Transform and return
46	
47	```javascript
48	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
49	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
50	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
51	```
52	
53	### Build a payload for a downstream node
54	
55	```javascript
56	return {
57	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
58	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
59	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
60	};
61	```
62	
63	### Error check from upstream
64	
65	```javascript
66	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
67	if (error) {
68	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
69	}
70	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
71	```
72	
73	### Reading a file-typed variable
74	
75	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
76	
77	```javascript
78	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
79	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
80	```
81	
82	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
83	
84	## Debug
85	
86	| Error | Cause | Fix |
87	| --- | --- | --- |
88	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
89	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
90	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
91	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
92	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
93	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
94	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
95

1	# HTTP Request Node — Connector Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when the target service has an IS connector and you want managed auth (OAuth / API key) handled by an existing IS connection.
4	
5	**Prerequisite:** a healthy IS connection for the target connector. Step 2 verifies this. If none exists, propose manual mode as the fallback and confirm the switch with the user before finalizing — do not switch modes without that confirmation.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–5 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Steps 2 and 3 reuse it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 3 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
17	
18	## Step 2 — Identify target connection
19	
20	**Connector mode only works if the connector supports the HTTP request activity** — verify by running `uip is connectors get "<target-connector-key>"` and checking the `HasHttpRequest` flag. If the flag is false, **STOP** — a connection cannot help. Use the recovery question below (switch to manual mode / skip / something else; the create-a-connection option does not apply) and do not switch modes without confirmation.
21	
22	```bash
23	uip is connections list "<target-connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
24	```
25	
26	`--all-folders` is mandatory for discovery. Selection rules, empty-result recovery, and ping verification live in the platform skill — do not duplicate them here.
27	
28	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md).
29	
30	Record the chosen connection's `Id` and `FolderKey` — Step 3 needs both.
31	
32	> **HTTP-specific recovery — no usable connection.** If platform-skill recovery yields nothing (empty after `--all-folders` + `--refresh`, user declines to create one), the HTTP node has unique fallback options. Ask the user to confirm the path — **manual mode is the recommended auto-fallback**, pre-selected, since it unblocks the node without a connection:
33	>
34	> - **Switch this node to manual mode** *(recommended)* — abandon this walkthrough and follow [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md). Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so this needs explicit confirmation.
35	> - **Create a new connection now** — `uip is connections create "<target-connector-key>"` starts the OAuth flow. User completes browser auth themselves, then re-run `uip is connections list` to pick up the new connection.
36	> - **Skip this node**.
37	> - **Something else**.
38	>
39	> Auto-try the fallback, but do not finalize a mode switch without the user's confirmation; do not invent a placeholder ID; do not skip the node without explicit selection. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md).
40	
41	## Step 3 — Configure the node
42	
43	> **STOP — open the platform skill before configuring.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, read [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md) and resolve every value you don't already have (IDs from names, required body fields, endpoint path, response shape).
44	>
45	> - **If the target connector is listed in that skill's `vendor-docs-registry.json`:** you MUST follow its **Step 0 (Ground Against the Vendor's API Docs)** — read the `docsUrl` + `notes` and confirm the exact endpoint with the `http-request` probe before running `node configure`. Pass the endpoint path verbatim: vendor method names can contain literal dots (Slack ``chat.postMessage`) — the dot is part of the path segment.
46	> - **If the connector is NOT listed:** the registry-grounding step does not apply — resolve missing values via the `http-request` probe / vendor docs as usual.
47	
48	```bash
49	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
50	  --detail '{
51	    "authentication": "connector",
52	    "targetConnector": "<target-connector-key>",
53	    "connectionId": "<target-connection-id>",
54	    "folderKey": "<folder-key>",
55	    "method": "GET",
56	    "url": "/api/endpoint",
57	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
58	  }' --output json
59	```
60	
61	> **Connector mode supports `application/json` request and response bodies only.**
62	
63	The CLI:
64	
65	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (connector, connectionId, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
66	- Auto-fills both `bodyParameters.path` and `bodyParameters.url` from the single `url` value you pass
67	- Generates `bindings_v2.json`
68	- Creates a connection resource file under `resources/solution_folder/connection/`
69	
70	**Dynamic values:** connector input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
71	
72	## Step 4 — (Optional) Response branches
73	
74	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 5 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
75	
76	## Step 5 — Wire edges
77	
78	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 4 entry). Wire `default` to the next node and `error` to a handler — without an `error` edge, a failed call faults the flow.
79	
80	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
81	
82	## Debug
83	
84	See [impl.md — Debug](impl.md#debug). For connector mode, the most common errors are `not_authed` / 401/403 (expired connection — ping it) and `Connection not found` (wrong connector key or connection ID — re-list).
85

1	# Variables and Expressions
2	
3	Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files.
4	
5	> **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow.
6	>
7	> `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors:
8	>
9	> - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107)
10	> - Invented `nodes.<id>.output` syntax
11	> - References to unknown variables or node IDs
12	> - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false`
13	>
14	> Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Table of contents
19	
20	- [Variables Overview](#variables-overview)
21	- [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals)
22	- [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes)
23	- [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates)
24	- [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes)
25	- [Expression System](#expression-system)
26	- [Available Globals](#available-globals)
27	- [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts)
28	- [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints)
29	- [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules)
30	- [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli)
31	- [Complete Example](#complete-example)
32	
33	---
34	
35	## Variables Overview
36	
37	Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections:
38	
39	```json
40	{
41	  "variables": {
42	    "globals": [],
43	    "nodes": [],
44	    "variableUpdates": {}
45	  }
46	}
47	```
48	
49	| Section | Purpose |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state |
52	| `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) |
53	| `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables |
54	
55	---
56	
57	## Workflow Variables (`globals`)
58	
59	Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role.
60	
61	### Directions
62	
63	| Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case |
64	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
65	| `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called |
66	| `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes |
67	| `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes |
68	
69	### Schema
70	
71	```typescript
72	{
73	  id: string              // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id}
74	  direction: "in" | "out" | "inout"
75	  type?: string           // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file"
76	  subType?: string        // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string")
77	  schema?: object         // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types
78	  defaultValue?: unknown  // Initial value (must match type)
79	  description?: string    // Human-readable description
80	  triggerNodeId?: string  // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows)
81	}
82	```
83	
84	### Examples
85	
86	**String input with default:**
87	```json
88	{
89	  "id": "customerName",
90	  "direction": "in",
91	  "type": "string",
92	  "defaultValue": "Unknown",
93	  "description": "Name of the customer to process"
94	}
95	```
96	
97	**Number output:**
98	```json
99	{
100	  "id": "totalAmount",

1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)](#project-structure-from-uip-maestro-flow-init)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
44	
45	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
46	
47	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by `uip maestro flow init` and packaging. Do not add them manually.
48	
49	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
50	
51	## Project structure (from `uip maestro flow init`)
52	
53	```
54	<ProjectName>/
55	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
56	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
57	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
58	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
59	├── operate.json            # runtime options
60	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
61	```
62	
63	## Node instance
64	
65	```json
66	{
67	  "id": "rollDice",
68	  "type": "core.action.script",
69	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
70	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
71	  "inputs": {
72	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
73	  },
74	  "outputs": {
75	    "output": {
76	      "type": "object",
77	      "description": "The return value of the script",
78	      "source": "=result.response",
79	      "var": "output"
80	    },
81	    "error": {
82	      "type": "object",
83	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
84	      "source": "=result.Error",
85	      "var": "error"
86	    }
87	  }
88	}
89	```
90	
91	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
92	
93	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
94	
95	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
96	>
97	> ```
98	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
99	> ```
100	>
101	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
102	
103	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
104	>
105	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
106	
107	### Instance-specific identity fields
108	
109	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
110	
111	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
112	|-------|---------|---------|
113	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
114	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
115	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
116	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
117

1	# HITL Node — Implementation
2	
3	Two node types implement human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Choose based on whether you need an inline form or an existing deployed app.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Option 1 — `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (Inline Schema — OOTB)
8	
9	This is the preferred option. No registry pull, no app publishing, no tenant dependency. Write the node directly into the `.flow` file as JSON.
10	
11	**Full implementation guide, JSON examples, and schema conversion rules:**
12	→ [`uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill — hitl-node-quickform.md](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-quickform.md)
13	
14	> **Note:** Skills are self-contained. This cross-skill reference is for documentation context only. The agent uses the `uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill to implement HITL nodes. This implementation guide is for implementation-phase topology resolution only — not for schema design or node writing.
15	
16	### Adding / Editing
17	
18	For add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). **Use `Edit` / `Write` for HITL node authoring.** Do not use the dedicated HITL CLI for this non-carve-out structural edit. Wire the `outcome-completed` port after adding the node.
19	
20	### Quick Reference
21	
22	**Node JSON (minimum viable):**
23	
24	```json
25	{
26	  "id": "hitlReview1",
27	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form",
28	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
29	  "display": { "label": "Invoice Review" },
30	  "inputs": {
31	    "schema": {
32	      "schemaId": "<uuid>",
33	      "fields": [
34	        { "id": "invoiceid", "label": "Invoice ID", "type": "text",   "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice.output.invoiceId" },
35	        { "id": "amount",    "label": "Amount",     "type": "number", "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice.output.amount" },
36	        { "id": "decision",  "label": "Decision",   "type": "text",   "direction": "output", "variable": "vars.decision" }
37	      ],
38	      "outcomes": [
39	        { "id": "approve", "name": "Approve", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true,  "action": "Continue" },
40	        { "id": "reject",  "name": "Reject",  "type": "string", "isPrimary": false, "action": "End" }
41	      ]
42	    },
43	    "recipient": { "channels": ["Email", "ActionCenter"], "connections": {}, "assignee": { "type": "group" } },
44	    "priority": "Low"
45	  },
46	  "outputs": {
47	    "output": {
48	      "type": "object",
49	      "description": "Task result data",
50	      "source": "=result",
51	      "var": "output",
52	      "properties": {
53	        "decision": { "type": "string" },
54	        "Action":   { "type": "string", "enum": ["Approve", "Reject"], "default": "Approve" }
55	      }
56	    },
57	    "status": {
58	      "type": "string",
59	      "description": "Task completion status",
60	      "source": "=result.Action",
61	      "var": "status",
62	      "enum": ["Approve", "Reject"],
63	      "default": "Approve"
64	    }
65	  }
66	}
67	```
68	
69	**Field format rules:**
70	- **Input fields**: `binding: "vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>"` (raw path, no `=js:$` prefix). No `variable` property on input fields.
71	- **Output fields**: `variable: "vars.<globalName>"` (`vars.` prefix required). No `binding`.
72	- **InOut fields**: both `binding` and `variable`, same formats as above.
73	- `schemaId` (not `id`) at the schema level — generate a fresh UUID.
74	- `typeVersion` — always `"1.0"` for `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`. **Do not run `registry get` to derive this value; do not use `"1.1"` or any other version.** The OOTB HITL node version is stable at `1.0`.
75	- No `model` block on node instances — only the definition carries it.
76	
77	**outputs block**: only `output` (with `properties` for output/inOut fields + `Action` outcome) and `status` (with `enum`/`default` from outcomes). No per-field `custom: true` entries.
78	
79	**Ports:** `input` (target) → `outcome-completed` (source, label: Completed)
80	
81	**Output variables:**
82	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — object with all `output` / `inOut` field values, keyed by **field `id`**
83	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldId}` — individual field value (e.g. `$vars.hitlReview1.output.decision`)
84	- `$vars.{nodeId}.status` — selected outcome name (e.g. `"Approve"`, `"Reject"`)
85	- `$vars.{globalId}` — workflow-global alias; `globalId` is `field.variable` with `vars.` stripped. **Do not use this in scripts — always use `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldId}` instead.**
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Option 2 — App-Based HITL (`uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app`)
90	
91	Use when there is an existing deployed Action Center app that should serve as the task form.
92	
93	### Discovery
94	
95	**CLI (primary path):**
96	
97	```bash
98	uip solution resources list --kind App --output json
99	```
100	
101	Returns all Action Center app types (`vB Action`, `workflow Action`, `Coded Action`, `JS Action`). Filter by app name. Then retrieve the configuration:
102	
103	```bash
104	uip solution resources get <key> --output json
105	```
106	
107	**Direct API fallback (if CLI unavailable):**
108	
109	```
110	GET {BASE_URL}/{ORG}/studio_/backend/api/resourcebuilder/solutions/{SOLUTION_ID}/resources/search
111	  ?kind=app&pageSize=25&projectKey={PROJECT_KEY}&includeSolutionResources=true
112	  &types=VB%20Action&types=Workflow%20Action&types=Coded%20Action&types=CodedAction&types=JS%20Action
113	```
114

116	
117	### Node JSON (Quick Reference)
118	
119	```json

121	  "id": "invoiceReview1",
122	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app",
123	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
124	  "display": { "label": "Invoice Review" },
125	  "inputs": {
126	    "recipient": { "channels": ["ActionCenter"], "connections": {}, "assignee": { "type": "group" } },
127	    "app": {
128	      "displayName": "Invoice Approval",
129	      "name": "Invoice Approval",
130	      "key": "<app.key>",
131	      "folderPath": "Shared",
132	      "inputSchema": {
133	        "type": "object",
134	        "properties": {
135	          "<paramName>": { "type": "string" }
136	        }
137	      },
138	      "outputSchema": {
139	        "type": "object",
140	        "properties": {
141	          "<outputName>": { "type": "string" }
142	        }
143	      }
144	    },
145	    "appInputBindings": {
146	      "<inputParamName>": "=vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>",
147	      "<inputParamName2>": "=metadata.InstanceId"
148	    },
149	    "schema": {
150	      "fields": [],
151	      "outcomes": [{ "id": "submit", "name": "Submit", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true, "action": "Continue" }]
152	    },
153	    "priority": "Medium"
154	  },
155	  "outputs": {
156	    "output": {
157	      "type": "object",
158	      "description": "Task result data",
159	      "source": "=result",
160	      "var": "output",
161	      "properties": {

163	      }
164	    },

167	      "description": "Task completion status",
168	      "source": "=result.Action",
169	      "var": "status",
170	      "enum": ["Submit"],
171	      "default": "Submit"
172	    }
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	**`typeVersion`** — fill in the version returned by `uip maestro flow registry get <appKey>` for the specific deployed app. Unlike QuickForm (always `"1.0"`), AppTask version varies per app definition.
178	
179	**`inputs.app`**: `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` are JSON Schema objects (`{ "type": "object", "properties": { ... } }`), **not arrays**.
180	
181	**`inputs.appInputBindings`** — maps app input parameter names to binding expressions. Format: `"=vars.<path>"` (with `=` prefix, no `js:`). Key = parameter name from `inputSchema.properties`. Without this, all input fields appear blank.

183	### If the app does not exist yet
184	
185	Note as `[CREATE NEW] <description>` in the node table and use `core.logic.mock` as a placeholder. The app itself is out of scope for this skill — use the `uipath-coded-apps` skill to build it.

189	## Common Pattern — Human-in-the-Loop
190	
191	```text
192	Manual Trigger -> RPA Process (extract) -> HITL (review) -> Decision (approved?) ->
193	  true: Script (submit) -> End
194	  false: End
195	```
196	
197	## Debug
198	
199	| Error | Cause | Fix |
200	| --- | --- | --- |
201	| Node type not found in registry (Option 2) | App not published or registry stale | If in same solution: `uip maestro flow registry list --local`. Otherwise: `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
202	| Task never completes | Human hasn't submitted the form | Check task assignment in Orchestrator |
203	| Output missing expected fields | App form doesn't match expected schema | Verify app form fields match what the flow expects |
204	| `outcome-completed` port unwired (Option 1) | Missing edge on output handle | Wire the `outcome-completed` output handle — an unwired `outcome-completed` blocks the flow indefinitely |
